title: World Court finds Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
h1: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time it has found a state responsible
description: The ICJ ruled Nov. 19, 2026, in The Gambia's case that Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention in 2017 and must compensate Rohingya and allow safe return.
standfirst: In a divided judgment read in The Hague on Thursday, the UN's top court held Myanmar responsible for genocide during the 2017 military campaign in Rakhine state. The ruling is binding, but the court has no way to enforce it on its own.
keywords: ICJ Myanmar genocide ruling, Gambia v Myanmar judgment 2026, Rohingya genocide International Court of Justice, Myanmar compensation Rohingya, Genocide Convention ruling
takeaways: The ICJ delivered its merits judgment on Nov. 19, 2026, in the case The Gambia filed in November 2019.
The AP reported the court found Myanmar forces killed about 10,000 Rohingya, and that the ruling passed 9-6.
Compensation will be set in later proceedings; about 1.2 million Rohingya refugees live in Bangladesh.
body: The International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday, Nov. 19, that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority, according to an Associated Press report published by PBS NewsHour. Court President Yuji Iwasawa read the judgment in The Hague. The AP said the decision was 9-6 and is the first time the court has found a country responsible for committing genocide.

The case grew out of the military's August 2017 "clearance" campaign in northern Rakhine state. According to the AP, the court concluded that Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, about 10,000 in all, and carried out widespread sexual violence, extreme violence against children and attacks on people fleeing. It rejected Myanmar's argument that the operation targeted insurgents.

The court ordered Myanmar to make a safe, voluntary and dignified return possible for Rohingya, to investigate and punish those responsible, and to pay compensation in an amount to be decided later. The court's case page lists the judgment alongside more than a dozen individual opinions, including a joint dissent signed by six judges, among them Vice-President Sebutinde.

The Gambia filed the case in November 2019 under the 1948 Genocide Convention. The court ordered provisional measures in January 2020, rejected Myanmar's objections in July 2022 and heard arguments on the merits in January 2026, Human Rights Watch noted ahead of the ruling. Eleven other countries were permitted to intervene.

ICJ judgments are final and binding, but if a state does not comply, the main recourse is the UN Security Council, which Human Rights Watch says has never used that power. Myanmar's government did not react immediately, the AP said. Gambia's justice minister, Dawda Jallow, said, "The victory belongs to the Rohingya." About 1.2 million Rohingya refugees remain in Bangladesh, mostly in camps in Cox's Bazar.

faq.q: Can the ICJ force Myanmar to comply?
faq.a: No. The ruling is binding, but the court cannot enforce it. A party can turn to the UN Security Council if Myanmar does not comply.

faq.q: Who brought the case against Myanmar?
faq.a: The Gambia filed the case in November 2019 under the 1948 Genocide Convention.
